title: Charlie Creath and memorizing repertoire
summary: Foster discusses Charlie Creath in St. Louis, his trumpet playing, and how bands memorized repertoire instead of reading.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: The last time we went up there, I think he went with Charlie Crith from St. Louis. Charlie Crith. Do you know him?
Oh, yes. He married his sister. Sister. Margaret.

Margaret. Margaret. Margaret of Margaret. That's what he stopped saying in St. Louis. I played with Charlie Crith quite often when I was up there. He used to play with those boys at the show for clubs sometimes.
How did Charlie Crith play? I heard he was a good blues player. Was he good on everything or just blues? How did he sound like? Well, he is good. He's a good trumpet.
Did he read a lot or was he a good head member?

I didn't see why he read too much unless he just had to memorize a whole lot. But he knew. That's why a lot of those fellas used to play just like we used to have a whole repertoire. And didn't use the music at all. We just rehearse and memorize it. Do a lot more, much more when you could memorize and just stick it to the music all the time.
